title: Decodability linter (build-time): cumulative grapheme set vs story words + heart-word whitelist
accept: Linter rejects a fixture story containing a word not decodable from the cumulative grapheme set at its level, reporting the story id, word, and the graphemes that are out of level.
The same fixture story passes once (a) the word is whitelisted as a heart word for that level, or (b) an earlier-or-equal level introduces the missing grapheme (both positive variants tested).

Cumulative grapheme set at level N = union of graphemes from all skills introduced at levels <= N (from scope-&-sequence data); decodability of a word is judged against its authored graphemePhonemeMap graphemes (test with digraph and silent-e words: 'ship', 'cake').
Heart words are per-level explicit whitelists ('that level's explicitly-tagged heart words'); a heart word whitelisted at level N is accepted at level N and above, not below (edge tests).
TongueTwisters are exempt: the linter skips twister content entirely (modeled-first content may use above-level words) — test feeds a twister with out-of-level words and expects zero findings.
A-8 length bounds checked as lint findings: sentence-level stories 3-8 words; paragraph-level stories 40-90 words across 1-3 pages (positive and violation tests).
Linter is a pure function library (story + scope-&-sequence data in, findings out) usable by both the pack-build CLI and tests — no I/O in this ticket's files.
pinned_design: Unit 3 pinned: the decodability linter is a build-time tool, not a runtime feature; it rejects any story containing a word not decodable from the cumulative grapheme set at its level unless whitelisted as a heart word for that level. §6 pinned constraint: a story at level N may only use words decodable with skills introduced at levels <= N, plus that level's explicitly-tagged heart words (common irregular words taught as exceptions). Unit 14 pinned: twisters are exempt from decodability linting. R5 is the risk this mitigates: every word checked against the level's cumulative grapheme set; human editor approves (human approval is process, outside the linter). Decodability judgment uses WordToken.graphemePhonemeMap (each grapheme cluster must be introduced by some skill at <= level, per scope-&-sequence data).
notes: Pure Dart, fully headless. Kept separate from pack-build-cli so the trickiest pipeline logic lands leaf-first. Scope-&-sequence fixture data only (real table is OQ-5). The mapping from PhonicsSkill to the graphemes it introduces must come from the scope-&-sequence data file format defined in phonics-engine's loader — coordinate via domain-models types, not by importing phonics-engine files (deps stay minimal; if a shared 'skill introduces graphemes' field is needed, it belongs in the scope-&-sequence data schema consumed from domain-models/fixtures).
